correctness.rationale: The Leibniz identity in characteristic two forces D(z)=0 and symmetric T on the e_i span, leaving arbitrary f. Squaring gives exactly T²=0, fT=0. Self-adjoint square-zero T has isotropic image W=imT and kerT=W^⊥, and for fixed W nondegenerate symmetric forms count possible T. In odd r, the anisotropic all-ones vector splits off a symplectic H; in even r the isotropic H has one-dimensional radical, giving the claimed two terms for I_r. Orthogonal congruence classes count S_s. For each T the f annihilators of W number q^(r−s); of them q^s already vanish on kerT, hence rank s versus s+1. Direct independent GF(2) enumeration of all derivation matrices for r=2,3 reproduced histograms (1,5) and (1,13,6), confirming low-degree indexing. This finite check is not universal proof.
